items.problem: Is the TPP1 TEL patch one binding surface?
items.answer: No - bipartite. E215 grips K78/R132, E168 grips R774, 20.26 A apart.

items.problem: Can a drug-like small molecule span both halves?
items.answer: No - and it is a class exclusion. 7.8 phenyls needed: MW ~683, logP ~11.

items.problem: What is the shortest path across the gulf?
items.answer: 25.54 A with a 119 deg bend and tortuosity 1.26; a straight line is blocked.

items.problem: Can an alpha-helix present the E168/E169/E171 triad?
items.answer: No - 2 of 3 at best. The segment is a kinked turn (psi +24.4 deg, CA168-CA171 7.68 A), not a helix.

items.problem: Can the triad be presented at all, in the native geometry?
items.answer: Yes - graft the two native segments. 3 of 3 to 0.02 A: DWEEKEF-GGGGG-FSLLPTE, E215 at 4.10 A from K78.

items.problem: Does a peptide HOLD that geometry?
items.answer: A covalent constraint EXISTS, and WP45 missed it by screening disulfides only. Over six chemistries spanning 3.5-12.5 A, W167-L211 passes reach, direction, clash and payload tests at 6.34 A with cos 0.98/0.09 - and the native indole/Leu contact there is already 3.50 A. But the staple buys only 2.8 kcal/mol of ordering against a 12-20 kcal/mol cost: residual 9.2 kcal/mol unpaid. Constraint found, energy still not balanced.
items.blocker: the remaining 6.36 kcal/mol even after a structured PAPAP linker and a second staple attempt - neither closes it, so a presenting scaffold is still required (PDB screening + loop modelling, unavailable here)

items.problem: Can each module solve only its own site, fully?
items.answer: 4 of 5 do. One site (S3) was declared unsolvable on a helix model that was wrong - corrected by P4/P5 - so the module result is retained but its premise is superseded.
items.blocker: the MD3 module needs rebuilding on the graft (P5), not on a helix

items.problem: Do merged modules stay stable together?
items.answer: 4 of 5 merges STABLE, 1 COLLAPSE-RISK, 1 REFUSED. The linker alone decides it: same two modules, -6.04 kcal/mol attraction when flexible.

items.problem: Can one groove be blocked and repaired at once?
items.answer: No - the merge engine refuses it by construction, with a stated reason.

items.problem: Is a structural alert a usable filter at all?
items.answer: No as a veto - proven unfixable, alert count caps at 0.70 balanced accuracy. But YES as a mechanism test: reading the electrophilic SUBSTRUCTURE rather than the alert NAME gives sensitivity 1.0 and specificity 1.0 (11/11) on a panel used by neither earlier WP. The failure was the vocabulary, and replacing it fixed it.

items.problem: Does the full gate stack accept approved drugs?
items.answer: No. 10/11 end-to-end on the third panel; the one miss is Lipinski rejecting atorvastatin (MW 559, logP > 5). That is a pre-existing gate defect inherited from WP43, not a reactivity failure - it is attributed, not blamed on the layer that was fixed.
items.blocker: Lipinski false rejection of large approved drugs; needs a rule that does not reject a marketed molecule at MW 559

items.problem: What is the experimental success rate?
items.answer: Unknown. N = 0 designs have been made, so the rate has no denominator.
items.blocker: synthesis and assay; no amount of computation supplies this

items.problem: Do any of these designs bind telomerase?
items.answer: Unknown - and it is reported as unknown rather than scored.

summary.answer_to_the_question: No. 8 of 16 sub-problems are solved, and all 8 are solved as CALCULATIONS. Zero are solved as evidence, because nothing has been made or measured. 3 are not solved, 3 are partial, and 2 cannot be answered by any computation here. The largest open item is still P6: WP47 found a real covalent constraint (W167-L211, 6.34 A) where WP45 had concluded none existed, but one staple buys 2.8 kcal/mol against a 12-20 kcal/mol ordering cost. WP48 then improved the construct (PAPAP linker, -2.84 kcal/mol) and still has 6.36 kcal/mol unpaid. A scaffold is still required.
what_would_change_it: P6: a scaffold search (needs PDB screening + loop modelling, not available here)
P10: an alert configuration that is sensitive AND specific on the controls
P11/P12: synthesis, then one binding and one activity measurement
